# Filter events

Boundary lets you control which events each sink receives by adding `allow_filters` and `deny_filters` predicates to a sink's configuration. This page explains how filters work and how to configure them.

## Requirements

- An event sink configured in the `events` stanza. Refer to [Configure event sinks](/boundary/docs/monitor/events/configure-sinks).
- Familiarity with Boundary's filter syntax. Refer to [Filtering and listing resources](/boundary/docs/filtering).

## How event filters work

Boundary emits several types of events: error, observation, system, and telemetry. It can format events as [cloudevents](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec) or [hclog](https://github.com/hashicorp/go-hclog) entries, encoded as JSON or text.

You can define any number of sinks to receive events. Each sink supports the `allow_filters` and `deny_filters` [common sink parameters](/boundary/docs/monitor/events/common):

- If any `allow_filters` predicate matches an event, Boundary includes the event in the sink.
- If any `deny_filters` predicate matches an event, Boundary excludes the event from the sink.

Both parameters use the standard [filter syntax](/boundary/docs/filtering) that Boundary uses elsewhere.

## Example events

The filters in this page select the following two events encoded as cloudevents-text. The first is a system event and the second is an observation event.

```json
{
  "id": "DU7u227Jhc",
  "source": "https://hashicorp.com/boundary/dev-controller/boundary-dev",
  "specversion": "1.0",
  "type": "system",
  "data": {
    "version": "v0.1",
    "op": "worker.(Worker).createClientConn",
    "data": {
      "address": "127.0.0.1:9201",
      "msg": "connected to controller"
    }
  },
  "datacontentype": "text/plain",
  "time": "2021-08-05T18:00:05.303435-04:00"
}
{
  "id": "s5ESg6CckX",
  "source": "https://hashicorp.com/boundary/dev-controller/boundary-dev",
  "specversion": "1.0",
  "type": "observation",
  "data": {
    "latency-ms": 202.995176,
    "request_info": {
      "id": "gtraceid_WiLnGzc2UHmNAYlcQ0sK",
      "method": "POST",
      "path": "/v1/auth-methods/ampw_1234567890:authenticate"
    },
    "start": "2021-08-05T18:00:34.032333-04:00",
    "status": 200,
    "stop": "2021-08-05T18:00:34.235335-04:00",
    "version": "v0.1"
  },
  "datacontentype": "text/plain",
  "time": "2021-08-05T18:00:34.235357-04:00"
}
```

## Filter events in a sink configuration

To limit a sink that receives every event type to only the events in the preceding example, add `allow_filters` to the sink configuration.

1. Open the Boundary configuration file.
1. Add the `allow_filters` parameter to the `sink` block.

   ```hcl
   sink "stderr" {
     name        = "all-events"
     description = "All events sent to stderr"
     event_types = ["*"]
     format      = "cloudevents-text"
     allow_filters = [
       "\"/data/request_info/path\" contains \":authenticate\"",
       "\"/data/op\" contains \".createClientConn\"",
     ]
   }
   ```

1. Restart Boundary.

To exclude events instead of including them, use `deny_filters` with the same syntax.

## Filter events with `boundary dev`

When you run `boundary dev`, pass filters with the `-event-allow-filter` and `-event-deny-filter` flags. You can specify each flag more than once.

```shell-session
$ boundary dev \
    -event-allow-filter '"/data/request_info/path" contains ":authenticate"' \
    -event-allow-filter '"/data/op" contains ".createClientConn"'
```

Double quotes are part of the filter syntax. When using the CLI, surround the filter with single quotes to avoid escaping the inner double quotes.
